draft.title: Finding an angle with trigonometry
card: When you know two sides of a right-angled triangle, you can find an angle. Start by naming the two known sides from the angle you want: opposite, adjacent or hypotenuse.
Choose sin, cos or tan, whichever ratio uses both of your known sides. Divide one side by the other to get a number.
Then use the inverse function on a calculator (\(\sin^{-1}\), \(\cos^{-1}\) or \(\tan^{-1}\)) to turn that number into the angle. It must match the ratio you chose.
Example: opposite \(= 3\) and adjacent \(= 4\), so use tan. \(\tan \theta = \frac{3}{4} = 0.75\), so \(\theta = \tan^{-1}(0.75) \approx 36.9^{\circ}\).
draft.remember: Divide the two known sides, then use the matching inverse function to get the angle.

a.q: A 10 m ladder leans against a wall and reaches 5 m up the wall. What angle does the ladder make with the ground?
a.why: The wall height is opposite the angle and the ladder is the hypotenuse, so use sin. \(\sin \theta = \frac{5}{10} = 0.5\), so \(\theta = \sin^{-1}(0.5) = 30^{\circ}\). Using \(\tan^{-1}(0.5)\) gives 26.6°, but tan needs the adjacent side, which is not given.
a.clue: Which two sides do you know, seen from the angle at the ground?

b.q: A steep driveway in Melbourne rises 1.2 m over a flat distance of 5 m. What is its angle of slope, to one decimal place?
b.why: The rise is opposite the angle and the flat distance is adjacent, so use tan. \(\tan \theta = \frac{1.2}{5} = 0.24\), so \(\theta = \tan^{-1}(0.24) \approx 13.5^{\circ}\). Using \(\sin^{-1}(0.24)\) gives 13.9°, but the 5 m is not the hypotenuse.
b.clue: The rise and the flat distance are opposite and adjacent.

check.summary: No problems found. Both answers check out: sin⁻¹(0.5) = 30° and tan⁻¹(0.24) ≈ 13.5°, the card example tan⁻¹(0.75) ≈ 36.9° is correct, and the distractors match common wrong-ratio or complementary-angle errors.
